title: findBindingSites finds no sites on RNA records: a U in the template never matches
description: findBindingSites documents its template as 'uppercase IUPAC as stored in a SeqRecord', and the readers keep U for RNA records. parseFasta sets molecule 'RNA' and keeps U when a sequence has U and no T (e.g. SILVA, RNAcentral or miRBase exports); the GenBank reader keeps U for RNA/rRNA/tRNA records. The primer side reads U as T, but the template side does not. The MATCH table is built only from IUPAC_DNA codes, so template 'U' is accepted by no primer base on either strand, and the exact indexOf seed never finds 'T' where the template has 'U'. Result: the universal 16S primer 515F gets zero sites on the RNA form of a real E. coli 16S fragment, silently. A user would conclude the primer does not bind. Primers designed on the same record also fail to bind it (see the designPrimer finding). Suggested fix: treat a template U as T, either via MATCH entries for 'U' equal to those of 'T' plus a U->T view for the seed search, or by normalising once.
expected: On the RNA record, the same single forward site as on the DNA form: { strand: 1, range: { start: 20, end: 39 }, annealedLength: 19, mismatches: 0, tailLength: 0, tm: 66.06 }.
actual: [] (no binding site). The DNA form gives the expected site.

title: designPrimer on an RNA record returns U-containing forward primers and a false 'IUPAC ambiguity' warning
description: Same root cause as the binding finding: the template's U is not read as T. designPrimer copies the top strand into forward primers unchanged, so on an RNA record the DNA primer is returned with U. Its ambiguity check (IUPAC_DNA[ch] === undefined) flags every candidate containing U as ambiguous. Consequences: (1) the forward primer to order reads 'GUGCCAGCAGCCGCGGUAAUAC' instead of 'GTGCCAGCAGCCGCGGTAATAC'; (2) the warning wrongly says the Tm is a mean over IUPAC expansions (the Tm, 66.51 °C, is in fact identical to the DNA case); (3) because every candidate is flagged, the 'avoid ambiguous lengths' preference can no longer tell real template N's from U's; (4) findBindingSites finds 0 sites for the designed primer on its own template. Reverse primers are correct, because reverseComplement maps U to A.
expected: sequence 'GTGCCAGCAGCCGCGGTAATAC' (as on the DNA form) and no ambiguity warning.
actual: sequence 'GUGCCAGCAGCCGCGGUAAUAC'; warnings ['The primer contains IUPAC ambiguity codes from the template; its Tm is the mean over their expansions.', 'Tm 66.5 °C is 6.5 °C from the target 60 °C within 18–30 nt.']; findBindingSites(record.seq, 'linear', designed primer) returns 0 sites.

title: Validation after toUpperCase() accepts ß/ſ/ﬅ/ﬆ as S/T bases and breaks length invariants and error messages
description: prepareSequence (tm.ts), prepare (analysis.ts) and the primer check in findBindingSites (binding.ts) all call String.prototype.toUpperCase() before validating characters. Four BMP characters upper-case into IUPAC letters, and the string length changes: ß (U+00DF) becomes SS, ſ (U+017F) becomes S, and ﬅ/ﬆ (U+FB05/FB06) become ST. These malformed inputs are silently accepted as extra S/T bases: tm(anneal + 'ß') equals tm(anneal + 'SS'), oligoGcContent('ﬆ') = 0.5, and hairpin() folds a sequence ending in 'ſ'. findBindingSites computes tailLength against the upper-cased length, which breaks the types.ts contract tailLength = primer.sequence.length − annealedLength. Error messages take the position from the upper-cased string but the character from the original, giving "position 2: 'undefined'" for 'ßX'. Fix: validate the original characters (e.g. /^[ACGTURYSWKMBDHVN]*$/i or a 128-entry table) before upper-casing.
expected: RangeError for every non-IUPAC input character, the types.ts tail/annealed length relation holds, and the error names the offending character.
actual: tm returns 63.05 °C; oligoGcContent('ﬆ') returns 0.5; hairpin returns a structure; site.annealedLength + site.tailLength = 22 for a 21-character primer; tm('ßX') throws "Not an IUPAC DNA character at position 2: 'undefined'".

title: designPrimer's warning misreports the searched lengths when a template N rules out longer primers
description: Candidates that contain a template ambiguity code are silently dropped from the pool whenever any unambiguous candidate exists. The Tm warning still reports the full minLength–longest window, and nothing tells the user that the ambiguity code, not the sequence composition, limited the length. In the reproduction, one N at template position 20 restricts the pool to 18–20 nt. The result is a 20-mer at 44.2 °C, 15.8 °C below target, with the warning 'within 18–30 nt', while the 30-mer covering the N has a mean Tm of 66.6 °C. A UI showing this warning tells the user the target is unreachable in 18–30 nt, which is false, so the user cannot tell what to fix (e.g. resolve the N or move the primer). This breaks the 'enough context in warnings' requirement for the UI.
expected: A warning naming the lengths actually considered (18–20 nt) and stating that an IUPAC code in the template (position 20) excluded the longer primers.
actual: warnings = ['Tm 44.2 °C is 15.8 °C from the target 60 °C within 18–30 nt.'] (the 20-mer at 44.2 °C is returned; lengths 21–30 were never offered and the N is not mentioned).

title: designPrimer is quadratic in maxLength, which has no upper bound
description: checkLengths only requires maxLength to be an integer >= minLength. designPrimer then evaluates every length from minLength to min(maxLength, available bases), and for each one re-slices, reverse-complements, re-validates and recomputes the Tm of the whole candidate, so the cost is O(maxLength²). A caller that passes a large value to mean 'no limit' (Infinity is rejected, so Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER is the natural choice) freezes the engine. Measured: 10 kb circular plasmid with maxLength = Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER: 3.1 s; 200 kb template with maxLength 5,000 / 20,000: 0.7 s / 12.0 s. On the 4.6 Mb genome it is effectively a hang. designPrimerPair inherits this, because it caps maxLength only at the target length. Fix: reject or clamp maxLength (e.g. to nnMaxLength or a documented limit such as 100–1000 nt), or update candidates incrementally.
expected: Either a RangeError for an unreasonable maxLength, or a result in well under 1 s (near-linear work).
actual: 3083 ms for one call on a 10 kb plasmid; 12,004 ms with maxLength 20,000 on a 200 kb template (quadratic growth).

title: tmRange's sampled min/max miss the true extremes by up to 2.5 °C (docs say 'slightly')
description:
Above TM_EXACT_EXPANSION_LIMIT (4,096 expansions), tmRange reports min/max over 2,048 random expansions plus one 'all-G/C' and one 'all-A/T' expansion. TmRange.exact documents that the true extremes 'may lie slightly outside [min, max]', and the implementer's report says 'slightly off'. Exhaustive enumeration shows much larger errors:
- ACGTNNNNNNNNACGTACGT: reported 50.14–69.24 °C vs true 47.88–70.73 °C (min off by 2.26 °C, max by 1.49 °C).
- NNNNNNNNNATGCATGCAT: min off by 2.52 °C.
- GGCCNNNNNNNNNGGCCAATT: off by 1.1 °C at both ends.
The extra 'extreme' expansions do not help: they choose poly-C / poly-A rather than the strongest or weakest stack arrangement. A UI that presents the range as the Tm spread of a degenerate primer (e.g. to choose an annealing temperature) would hide variants that melt 2.5 °C lower. The spec allows sampling, but these errors are far from 'slight' and exact extremes are computable (a fractional-programming search over a 4-state nearest-neighbour DP, with palindromic expansions handled separately). At minimum, the docs should state the real error.
expected: Reported min/max contain (or come within a documented small tolerance of) the true extremes: true range 47.88–70.73 °C.
actual: Reported range 50.14–69.24 °C: r.min − trueMin = 2.26 °C, trueMax − r.max = 1.49 °C.

title: findBindingSites silently finds no sites on RNA records (template U never matches)
description:
The binding finder can only match A, C, G, T and the other IUPAC letters in the template. It builds its MATCH table from IUPAC_DNA, which has no 'U', and the fast path uses `template.indexOf` with patterns that contain T. The data model and the project's own parsers keep U in RNA records: types.ts only converts U to T for DNA records, `parseFasta` turns 'U without T' into an RNA record that keeps U, and genbank-sequence.ts states 'RNA keeps U'. The binding docs say the template is 'uppercase IUPAC as stored in a SeqRecord'.

As a result, any site whose annealed region covers a U is dropped without a warning. A 15-nt or longer site almost always contains a U, so on an RNA record practically every site disappears. A typical victim is a reverse-transcription primer on an RNA transcript. The sibling seq/search.ts module reads target U as T, so the two modules disagree. (Lowercase templates are a listed known limitation; U is not.)
expected: One site on the RNA record, the same as on its DNA version: strand -1, range {start: 80, end: 105}, annealedLength 25. Alternatively, U should be read as T in the template, as seq/search.ts does.
actual: `[]`. Vitest reports: AssertionError: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0. A forward primer (ATGGCTAGCAAAGGAGAAGAACT, found at 17..40 on DNA) also gives [] on the RNA record.

title: designPrimer on an RNA record returns a U-containing primer and a false 'IUPAC ambiguity codes' warning
description:
Candidate primers are cut straight from the template (`sliceRange(...).toUpperCase()`) without converting U to T. Because `IUPAC_DNA['U']` is undefined, every candidate on an RNA record is marked 'ambiguous'. That has three effects:
- The rule that avoids ambiguity codes is switched off.
- The result carries the warning 'The primer contains IUPAC ambiguity codes from the template; its Tm is the mean over their expansions', which is false: the Tm is exact, because tm() reads U as T.
- The forward primer comes back as an RNA string. If ordered as written, the U letters would usually be made as deoxyuridine, which uracil-intolerant proofreading polymerases do not read through.

Reverse primers happen to come out as DNA, because reverseComplement maps U to A.
expected: The same design as on the DNA version of the template: sequence 'GCTAGCAAAGGAGAAGAACTTTTCAC', range 20..46, Tm 60.79 °C, warnings [].
actual: Sequence 'GCUAGCAAAGGAGAAGAACUUUUCAC' (Tm 60.79 °C), with warnings ['The primer contains IUPAC ambiguity codes from the template; its Tm is the mean over their expansions.']. Vitest reports: AssertionError: expected 'GCUAGCAAAGGAGAAGAACUUUUCAC' not to match /U/.

title: G/C-clamp preference makes designPrimer leave the ±2.5 °C window although an in-window length exists
description:
The spec asks for 'Tm within ±2.5 °C of target when possible'. designPrimer instead prefers a primer ending in G or C whenever its Tm is at most 1 °C further from the target, and never checks the ±2.5 °C window. When the closest length is 1.5–2.5 °C away, the clamped choice can land 2.5–3.5 °C away. The warning it then emits, '... from the target ... within 18–30 nt', suggests no closer length existed, which is false.

The module's own test avoids this case: it only checks designs where some candidate is within 1.5 °C. On the repository's real plasmids (every gap, both directions, targets 55/60/65 °C) this happens in 79 of 26,166 designs on pBR322 and 34 of 16,116 on pUC19. It also happened in 9 of 3,000 random templates.

Example: the reverse primer with its 5' end at gap 83 of pBR322 J01749, default target 60 °C. Candidate Tms: 18 nt 62.24 °C (no clamp), 19 nt 61.86 °C (no clamp), 20 nt 62.77 °C (clamp). Because 0.90 ≤ 1, the 20-mer is chosen.

Suggested fix: only prefer the clamp while it stays inside the ±2.5 °C window, or when the best unclamped length is already outside it.
expected: A primer within ±2.5 °C of 60 °C, for example the 19-mer ACGGTGCCTGACTGCGTTA (61.86 °C). If the clamped 20-mer is kept, the warning should not imply that no closer length existed.
actual: The 20-mer ACGGTGCCTGACTGCGTTAG (Tm 62.77 °C, 2.77 °C from the target), with warning ['Tm 62.8 °C is 2.8 °C from the target 60 °C within 18–30 nt.']. Vitest reports: AssertionError: expected 2.765250308187376 to be less than or equal to 2.5.

title: endStability reports found=true for a structure in which seq1's 3'-terminal base is unpaired
description:
`endStability` is documented as the 'most stable duplex between seq1 and seq2 in which the 3'-terminal base of seq1 is paired'. `analyzePrimer.selfEndDimer` uses the same 3'-end mode internally.

When seq1's 3' base cannot pair with any base of seq2 (its complement is absent, or it is an ambiguity code), the code copies a primer3 fallback (thal.ts: `if (!isFiniteNumber(bestG)) bestI = bestJ = 1`). It then reports the structure ending at seq1's 5'-terminal base. So `found` is true, `pairs` is [[0, 9]] (the 5' G, not the 3' A), Tm is −277.9 °C and ΔG is +1.97 kcal/mol.

The numbers match primer3-py: `calc_end_stability('GGGGGCCCCCA','GGGGGCCCCC')` gives structure_found=True, tm=−277.93, dg=1967.85. The `pairs` array is HHereditas' own addition, though, and it shows a 3'-end structure with no 3'-end pair. A UI that draws or flags 3'-end dimers would show a meaningless one.

Suggested fix: return found=false when no alignment pairs the 3' base in end1 mode, or document the primer3 quirk on endStability and SecondaryStructure.
expected: Either found=false (no structure pairs the 3'-terminal base of seq1), or a structure whose pairs include index 10, as the documentation promises.
actual: {found: true, tm: -277.9275859468325, dG: 1.967854999993797, dH: 0.2, dS: -5.69999999998, pairs: [[0, 9]]}. Vitest reports: AssertionError: expected false to be true.

title: With maxMismatches ≥ 1, accidental tail matches turn a perfect site of a 5'-tailed primer into a mismatched site with a higher Tm
description: A mismatch is accepted whenever the next two primer bases toward the 5' end match (RESUME_MATCHES = 2). For a primer with a non-annealing 5' tail (restriction-site or Gibson tails are routine in cloning), this happens by chance about 1 time in 16. The site whose 3' region matches perfectly is then reported with a spurious mismatch, a longer annealed region that reaches into the tail, a shorter tail, and a Tm computed over the extended region as if the mismatch were a match. So raising the tolerance changes how a perfect site is reported. A UI using that Tm to choose an annealing temperature gets a value several °C too high. The default (maxMismatches 0) is unaffected. The Python brute-force oracle uses the same rule, so the oracle tests cannot catch this. The implementer's report says the two-base rule was chosen to avoid false tail mismatches; it reduces them but does not remove them.
expected: The site is reported the same way as with maxMismatches 0: range {start: 24, end: 46}, annealedLength 22, mismatches 0, tailLength 10, Tm 58.38 °C. The non-annealing tail should not be absorbed into the site because of a two-base chance match.
actual: range {start: 21, end: 46}, annealedLength 25, mismatches 1, tailLength 7, Tm 61.32 °C (+2.9 °C). In the random-tail experiment, 6.5% of perfectly matching tailed primers were changed this way, with Tm inflated by up to 12.5 °C (14.3 °C with maxMismatches 2).

title: findAllBindingSites is all-or-nothing: one primer that throws discards every other primer's sites
description: findAllBindingSites calls sitesOnCanonicalTemplate for each primer with no per-primer error handling. If one primer throws (more than maxSites sites, e.g. a degenerate primer on a large template, or an invalid character), the whole call throws and the UI gets no sites for any primer in the document. The TSDoc of findAllBindingSites does not mention that it can throw or that the result is all-or-nothing; only findBindingSites documents its throws. With default options, a 20-nt all-N primer on a 60 kb template (a large plasmid, fosmid or phage) is enough to trigger it.
expected: The site of primer 'good' is returned, and the primer that exceeds maxSites is reported per primer (for example, a per-primer error list). At minimum, findAllBindingSites should document that one failing primer aborts the whole call.
actual: RangeError: "Primer 'random-20' has more than 100000 binding sites; it is too degenerate or too short for this template (raise maxSites to list them all)." No sites are returned for any primer, including 'good'.

title: analyzePrimer validates maxLoop and temperatureCelsius only for primers of 60 nt or less
description: analyzePrimer calls thalConditions(options), which validates maxLoop (integer 0..30) and temperatureCelsius (finite), only inside `if (s.length <= THAL_MAX_ALIGN)`. The same invalid options therefore throw a RangeError for a 20-nt primer but are silently accepted for an 80-nt primer. A UI with a bad structure setting will see errors for some primers and not others, depending only on primer length.
expected: A RangeError for maxLoop 99 and for temperatureCelsius NaN, whatever the primer length, as for the 20-nt primer.
actual: Both calls on the 80-nt primer return normally (hairpin, selfDimer and selfEndDimer are undefined); the same options throw a RangeError for the 20-nt primer.

title: Hairpin/dimer calls inside the documented input domain block for up to 14–16 s, about 4–5× primer3 on the worst case
description: heterodimer and endStability accept one sequence of at most 60 nt and the other of up to THAL_MAX_SEQ = 10,000 nt. That is the natural 'check this primer against the template' use case. A synchronous call on a low-complexity partner blocks for 12–16 s, against 3.4 s for primer3-py on the same input. Typical inputs are smaller but still slow: a random 60-mer vs a random 10 kb sequence takes about 1 s; GC- or AT-repeat 60 × 10 kb takes 3.0–3.1 s (primer3: 1.0–1.1 s). A 60-nt hairpin takes 16–19 ms and a 60-nt homodimer 33–37 ms (primer3: 0.8 ms and 5 ms). The spec sets no performance target for these checks, so this is minor. Still, the input domain allows calls that look like a hang in an interactive UI, and the report's '0.02–3.6 ms per call' understates this.
expected: A call inside the documented limits completes in a time comparable to primer3 (3.4 s for this worst case), or the accepted input size is bounded or documented for interactive use.
actual: 14,285 ms in this run (16,344 ms in another); endStability on the same pair took 12,209 ms. The result itself (tm 102.31 °C) agrees with primer3.

title: A primer whose 3' anchor is all N, with mismatches allowed, takes 1.8–3.5 s on the 4.6 Mb genome (target < 1 s)
description: When maxMismatches >= 1, the exact seed is only the 3' anchor: seedLength = anchor, 5 nt by default (binding.ts line 180). Primers built for random priming end in N bases, for example SISPA/WTA primers such as FR26RV-N 'GTTTCCCAGTCACGATANNNNNNNNN' (Djikeng et al. 2008). For these, seedRegexSource() builds the pattern [ACGTRYSWKMBDHVN]{5}, which matches every template position. candidatePositions() then yields all 2 × 4.6 M positions through re.exec and a generator, and each one is walked. With default options (maxMismatches 0) the seed is 15 nt and takes about 45 ms; with maxMismatches 1 the search becomes a regex scan of the whole genome. This is 2–4× slower than the anchor3: 0 path the implementer measured, so the report's '474 ms worst case' is not the worst case. Only primers with a degenerate 3' anchor are affected: normal primers took 22–877 ms for every anchor3 from 0 to 5 with 1–3 mismatches, and a primer with 3 trailing N took 169 ms. Possible fixes: seed by pigeonhole on the non-degenerate bases of the minAnneal window (with at most m mismatches, one of m+1 disjoint segments must match exactly), or skip the regex and loop over positions directly when the seed accepts every base.
expected: One primer on the 4.6 Mb E. coli genome in under 1 s (spec target). This is the case for the same primers with default options (about 45 ms) and for non-degenerate primers with any anchor3 and up to 3 mismatches (22–877 ms).
actual: Three runs on an idle 32-core machine: FR26RV-N with {maxMismatches: 1} took 3531, 2552 and 2408 ms (28,210 sites; maxMismatches 2 took 3.4 s). 'ACGATCGGATCCTTAGNNNNN' with {maxMismatches: 1, computeTm: false} took 2218, 1993 and 1843 ms for only 42 sites. Each run failed with 'AssertionError: expected 2864.12 to be less than 1000' or similar.

title: 'owczarzy2008' throws 'no free cations' when monovalent = 0 and Mg2+ <= dNTP, but its own free-Mg2+ model gives a finite Tm
description: resolveTmConditions (tm.ts lines 143–145) applies primer3's rule 'free Mg2+ = Mg2+ − dNTP' to every salt-correction method. It throws when monovalentMilliMolar is 0 and divalentMilliMolar <= dntpMilliMolar. The 'owczarzy2008' method uses a different model, documented in SaltCorrectionMethod and owczarzy2008Correction: free Mg2+ comes from the Mg2+:dNTP association constant Ka = 3×10^4 M^-1 (Owczarzy 2008), and the result should match Biopython Tm_NN(saltcorr=7). Under that model some Mg2+ is always free. At 1.5 mM Mg2+ and 1.5 mM dNTP, free Mg2+ is (−1 + √181)/(6×10^4) M ≈ 0.21 mM; at 1.0 mM Mg2+ and 1.2 mM dNTP it is ≈ 0.10 mM. The Tm is therefore defined, and Biopython returns it. HHereditas rejects these conditions with an error message that is wrong for this model. The same RangeError reaches designPrimer, findBindingSites (computeTm) and analyzePrimer when called with these conditions. Only conditions without monovalent ions are affected: with any monovalent ions, 'owczarzy2008' matched Biopython exactly on 2,639 fresh wide-grid cases, including dNTP > Mg2+.
expected: 57.28 °C and 55.39 °C, the published Owczarzy 2008 model as implemented by Biopython saltcorr=7, which 'owczarzy2008' says it matches.
actual: Both calls throw RangeError: 'Tm conditions contain no free cations (monovalent = 0 and Mg2+ <= dNTP)' (tm.ts:144).
